target_customer: Independent retailers buying wholesale and the brands selling to them
problem: Independent shops found products slowly and carried inventory risk, while small brands struggled to reach and finance retailers.
business_model: Marketplace take rate on wholesale orders, plus retailer net terms and capital

founders.name: Max Rhodes
founders.background_notes: Tested the early product in retail shops with the founding designer.

technical_complexity.rationale: A two sided marketplace with machine learning matching, payments and risk on net terms. Standard engineering with credit risk as the hard part.

defensibility.rationale: Two sided liquidity of brands and retailers and financing terms made it harder to replicate. Shopify's Handshake and Tundra later faded.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Shopify's Handshake wholesale product was reported retired in 2023 and Shopify was rumored in July 2026 to be in acquisition talks, unconfirmed.

market_need_then: No dated 2017 demand source was found. Company framing says independent retail faced decades old wholesale obstacles.

branding.name_origin: First called Indigo Fair. A 2021 interview with the founding designer says the team liked that Faire stayed close to Indigo Fair while celebrating the doers and makers.
branding.domain_note: Uses faire.com, acquisition history not found.

identity.logo: Wordmark, brand pages published for sellers

branding.brand_signature: Faire as a celebration of independent makers

rebrands.why: Per founding designer interview, closer to the original while more celebratory of customers. Date comes from a weaker secondary site (February 2018).

branding.community_and_virality: Faire hosts brand pages and a seller blog on naming. No fan or meme evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Dominant wholesale marketplace brand for independent retail with hundreds of thousands of retailers, though no source credits the name itself for growth.

outcome_analysis: Faire built a wholesale marketplace for independent retail and rose to a 12.6 billion valuation in 2022. It cut 20 percent of staff in November 2023 and roughly 250 more later, then employees sold shares at 5.2 billion in November 2025. Fortune reported in November 2026 that it is eyeing an IPO, and acquisition talks with Shopify were rumored but unconfirmed.
notes: Company website returned HTTP 403 to the fetch tool and was not worked around, so no site description was read. The 2022 round amount (about 596M per Forge) is unverified, so amount is null; the 12.6B valuation is from TechCrunch's 2023 article. Dec 2018 round was reported as Series B and C together. Series A in January 2018 and the 2019 Series D are only in aggregators and not recorded. Shopify acquisition talks come from secondary outlets and are a rumor. No competitor source dated near 2017 was found; Handshake and Tundra statuses come from SEO blogs.
